tip: Turkish good-wishes often take the plural. Yolculuklar is the plural of yolculuk (journey); iyi yolculuklar means have a good trip.
The suffix -ce turns an adjective into a manner adverb. Güzel means nice, güzelce means nicely.
The suffix -la/-le means with and builds manner adverbs. Heyecan is excitement, heyecanla means excitedly.
A position word like karşısında (across from) needs the owner in the genitive: parkın karşısında means across from the park.
Güle güle is said by the person staying to the one leaving. The one departing says hoşça kal or hoşça kalın instead.
Geçmiş olsun is a fixed get-well phrase, literally may it be past; you say it to anyone sick or in trouble.
For pleased to meet you Turkish uses the past tense: memnun oldum is literally I became pleased.
A final k softens to ğ before a vowel ending. Sokak plus the -a ending becomes sokağa, meaning to the street.
Kusura bakmayın is a set apology, literally don't look at the fault, meaning no offense or excuse me.
Past continuous stacks -yor plus -du. Bekliyor (is waiting) becomes bekliyorduk, we were waiting.
To say need to, use the verb as a noun with a personal ending plus lazım. Düşünmem lazım means I need to think.
A verb becomes an object with -ma plus the accusative. Oynamayı öğretti means taught the playing, that is, taught how to play.
Adjectives and nouns are negated with the separate word değil, not a suffix. Hazır değilim means I'm not ready.
The accusative marks a definite object. Tansiyonumu (my blood pressure) ends in -u because it's the specific thing measured.
The -ip ending chains verbs that share one final tense. Buluşup yedik means met up and ate; only yedik carries the past.
Future tense is -acak/-ecek. Yaz (write) plus -acak gives yazacak, will write.
X of Y takes two suffixes: -in on the owner, -i on the thing. Dersin konusu means the lesson's subject.
Yüzünden means because of and is used for unwanted causes. Yağmur yüzünden means because of the rain.
Henüz plus a negative past verb means not yet. Henüz pasaportumu almadım means I haven't gotten my passport yet.
Kadar after a place in the dative means as far as. Ormana kadar means all the way to the forest.
The aorist -ir marks habits and general truths. Pişirir means bakes, as in bakes fresh bread every morning.
Ordinals add -üncü/-ıncı. Üç is three, üçüncü is third, as in üçüncü katında, on the third floor.
Çünkü (because) is unusual for Turkish: it sits before its reason clause. Çünkü zamanım vardı means because I had time.
The suffix -malı/-meli means must or should. Al (get) plus -malıyım gives almalıyım, I must get.
The ending -dir gives a statement a general, factual tone. Meyvedir means is a fruit, stated as a plain fact.
The ablative -dan/-den means from. Fırın (bakery) plus -dan gives fırından, from the bakery.
